# Context before the first check

This is an informed public-source boundary study for the ordinary #80 decision
https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/issues/80#issuecomment-6009479668.
The author is a Codex subagent with prior repository, Issue and code access;
no external model is invoked. Exact deployed model identifier and sampling
settings are unavailable. This is not a blind benchmark or user success rate.
The author has read the authoring procedure, actual Issue #80 and its ordinary
maintainer decision, common runtime/static call checks, relevant current type,
source and primitive Reference, Boolean/Unit example records, and the concurrently
authored functional-boundary.md draft before writing these projects. Reading
that draft is design context, not an independent specification review or adoption.

Ten complete first projects specify schema 2 and constitutional edition 2026.
The sources are independently authored from desired contracts rather than copied
from the implementation. Four positive controls and six deliberate adversarial
controls use zero through two source quantum bits. They share attempt-01 as one
pre-check experiment inventory; negative controls are not failed repairs.
No closure grammar rejection is presented as an owner-capture proof. The tuple
controls exercise actual resolved runtime/local provider categories instead.

Predictions are recorded before checking in predictions-before.json. Exact
mathematical expectations use X|0>=|1>, X squared=I and destructive Z observation;
these checks do not compare amplitudes, arbitrary references or scalar phase.
Diagnostic fragments are predictions with stage uncertainty; actual outputs decide
whether the intended boundary is reached. Earlier rejection does not prove a
later owner, provider, lowering or evidence condition. Empty main in open Unit
controls cannot execute their open quantum bodies.

The source-study baseline is 5bcc36f868fdddc4f68d1d715b83ad8e8aeeb726.
It is distinct from trusted constitutional continuity base
faa5cfb5e7ea1cf3b39a43b80f7f2345e89197c2. The first check used the source-study
baseline inadvertently as a continuity comparison; that actual result is preserved
separately and is not independent continuity evidence. Before writing or checking
these sources, the author reran the checker with the trusted faa5 base: PASS.
QS-2026-01, PR-2026-01, RS-2026-01 and EXACT-2026-01 remain binding with their
broader proof/enforcement duties pending. QS-QLV1-OWNERSHIP-2026-01 and
QS-QLV1-SCOPE-2026-01 remain protected for the exact original ordinary decoded
QLV1 root scope and premises. No new interpretation, guarantee, formal discharge,
release approval, proof replay or constitutional certification is claimed.

The existing CLI /private/tmp/qleisli-bounded-validation-target/debug/qleisli
has SHA-256 bd9219f7847f1a7a52a3bd1346d39e8455edf0988e04582595471ae439b5feef.
The explicitly selected native checker lean-kernel/.lake/build/bin/qleisli-kernel
has SHA-256 39effde0f152a2c926fcea3a7f99fc2f25f9de65906be2b8c527508353c90c85.
The observer will set QLEISLI_KERNEL explicitly and verify both executable hashes
before and after each actual command. These identify selected bytes, not a proof
of compiled-HEAD provenance or native-child completion. No build, download,
maximum-size generation or existing source change is performed. No qlippy/qargo
consumer integration is tested; it is explicitly excluded by the maintainer.
Corpus, standard library, examples and generic QFT are outside this study.
